documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its Q4 and FY26 financial and operational results, achieving its highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112 percent of installed capacity. Management highlighted a gross refining margin of $9.2 per barrel for the full financial year and $13.75 per barrel for the fourth quarter. The company announced a total dividend of INR62 per share for the year, including an interim dividend of INR8 and a recommended final dividend of INR54 per share. Furthermore, management outlined ongoing capital expenditure plans, including INR1,600 crores for Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS projects and INR400 crores for retail outlet endeavors. Management stated that the refinery achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT (99.5% of installed capacity) for the year and 2.974 MMT (113% of installed capacity) in Q4 FY25.

demand_outlook.claim: Motor spirit in the southern market has a clear shortfall where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Motor spirit demand growth in the southern market is projected around 4% to 5% against national projections of 6%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%.

demand_outlook.claim: High-speed diesel demand in the southern market is forecasted to grow at 3% compared to 2.5% nationally.
demand_outlook.quote: HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The company stated that project execution for Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS has started in full swing with all approvals in place.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: Management noted that the retail outlet endeavor involving 300 licenses has started, with significant commissioning expected during the year.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The management reported that the LOBS project requires INR1,600 crores and the retail outlet project requires INR400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The company spent Rs. 673 crores as capex for the current financial year.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL installed 1.04 MW capacity of ground-mounted and rooftop solar systems on plant area buildings.
capex_expansion.quote: 1.04 MW capacity of Ground Mounted and Roof top solar system on plant area buildings

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for quarter 4 was recorded at $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: Management stated that the core GRM for the fourth quarter was $10.3 per barrel.
The company reported a forex loss of approximately INR200 crores for the quarter and around INR350 crores for the whole year.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: The full year GRM for 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: The inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: Fuel and loss for the year came down to 8.51%.
margins_costs.quote: I must place it that if you remember our Energy Indexes and our Fuel and Loss Indexes were quite high 2-3 years back and we went to a roadmap where we said on a sustained basis, we will bring it down to very efficient levels and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

margins_costs.claim: The MBN is around 72.0 and the best energy intensity index of 87.4 was clocked in fiscal 2024-25.
margins_costs.quote: The MBN is at around 72.0. The best EII figure of 87.4 has been clocked in the current year, 2024-25.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported a Gross Refining Margin of $3.40/bbl for 9M FY2024-25 compared to $8.64/bbl in FY2023-24.
CPCL recorded net operating expenditure of Rs 945 crore in 9M FY2024-25.
CPCL incurred interest expense of Rs 165 crore in 9M FY2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 million metric tons, which is equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: During the fourth quarter, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, representing 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel and 1.318 MMT of petrol.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

orders_capacity.claim: The highest ever annual distillate yield of 79.1% was achieved during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved the highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT during the financial year.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT, overcoming previous record of 404 set in 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of its installed capacity during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year and if you take that into consideration , you will find that this performance is quite comparable to the previous year's performance where CPCL clocked 111% capacity utilization

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput for Q4 FY25 was 2.974 MMT, representing 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL processed crude throughput of 7,480 TMT during 9M FY2024-25.

capital_allocation.claim: The company's gross leverage position or debt-to-equity stands at 0.18 compared to 0.39 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: On a gross basis, borrowings are INR1,900 crores, while net borrowings are INR973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: The company reported its capex for the current year at INR856 crores compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity ratio as of March 31, 2025, stood at 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Absolute debt stood at Rs. 3,100 crores as of March 31, 2025, compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as of March 31, 2024.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: Net worth was recorded at Rs. 7,939 crores as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL reported a net worth of Rs 7,491 crore as of 9M FY2024-25.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management highlighted that uncertainties due to logistical constraints and the volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge to operations.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL incurred an exchange variation loss of Rs 122 crore in 9M FY2024-25.
CPCL recorded a CST under recovery of Rs 246 crore in 9M FY2024-25.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the total capex of INR2,000 crores for LOBS and retail outlets will happen over a period of 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: Management noted that in the first six months, they do not see any major maintenance and inspection.
management_commitments.quote: First, reply to you , in the first 6 months, we don't see any M&I.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the ongoing study for low-cost debottlenecking is expected to get completed in the coming financial year '26-'27.
management_commitments.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

management_commitments.claim: Maintenance capex is expected to remain in the range of Rs. 200 to Rs. 250 crores.
management_commitments.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

management_commitments.claim: Without the LOBS project, normal maintenance capex for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
